part.text: Found it — there was a logic bug in my implementation. Since the continuation bit is part of each byte, it can't be set before reversing the group order. The groups must be collected without the continuation bit, reversed, and then the continuation bit must be set on all bytes except the last one:

My reversal logic was wrong — the continue bit was set based on remaining groups before reversal, putting it on the wrong bytes after reversing. The fix collects raw 7-bit groups, reverses, then sets the continue bit on all but the last. Re-running:

part.text: The rerun was up-to-date so no test lines printed. Let me confirm from the test report:

All 26 tests pass with 0 failures. The implementation is complete in `src/main/java/VariableLengthQuantity.java`:

- **`encode`**: For each number, extracts the 7-bit groups least-significant-first (using an unsigned `>>> 7` shift), reverses them into most-significant-first order, then sets the high continue bit (`0x80`) on every group except the last. Each byte is rendered as a lowercase `0x`-prefixed hex string.
- **`decode`**: Shifts each byte's low 7 bits into an accumulator; when a byte has the continue bit clear, the accumulated value is emitted. If the input ends mid-sequence (continue bit still set), it throws `IllegalArgumentException("Invalid variable-length quantity encoding")`.

The only change made was to the solution file — tests and build files were left untouched.
